title: Manasseh, King of Judah
lead: Son of Hezekiah and king of Judah for 55 years, about 697–642 BC, the longest reign of any king of Judah. Kings makes him the worst of all and the cause of the exile; Chronicles tells that he repented in captivity and was restored. (For the tribe and the son of Joseph, see Joseph.)

sections.b: Besides 2 Kings 21 and 2 Chronicles 33, Manasseh is named in Jeremiah 15:4, where God says the people will be made a horror to all kingdoms because of what he did in Jerusalem, and in Matthew 1:10 among Jesus' ancestors. The penitential Prayer of Manasseh, written in Greek or Hebrew some centuries later, appears in the Apocrypha and in the Orthodox Bible.
sections.refs: 2 Kings 21:1–18; 2 Chronicles 33:1–20; Jeremiah 15:4; Matthew 1:10; Prayer of Manasseh
